goal: Speed up elliptic curve signing by enabling hardware-accelerated SHA256 in libsecp256k1
Brings signing performance gains to users running on CPUs with dedicated SHA extensions
reviewability: Ready for review; no known blockers or pending changes to invalidate review
agreement: Broad concept support across several contributors and maintainers
Verified by differential testing across 20,000 cryptographic operation rounds (fametrano)
Reviewed and approved after addressing context separation and startup questions (theStack, w0xlt)
Unanswered suggestion to clone the signing context to avoid a second self-test (fametrano)

categories.name: utils
why: P2 because it speeds up cryptographic signing operations on CPUs with hardware SHA extensions
ECDSA signing drops by roughly 13% to 15% and Schnorr signing drops by 3% to 7%
Verification gains are negligible, keeping the performance benefits focused on signing workloads
